## claude.ai Supabase
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

Build is green. Here's where things stand.

## The card is already fixed in your working tree

This Trello card has two halves, and both are addressed by uncommitted work sitting on `main`:

**"There is no way to add multiple harvests from moderator for a produce"** — this was the real bug. The farmer's Edit Harvest form had a harvest-logging panel; the moderator's had a single "Latest harvest date & time" input, so a moderator could only ever overwrite one date, never log a second pick. The fix extracted that panel into a shared `src/components/HarvestManager.tsx` and mounted it in the moderator's edit form, so both surfaces now render literally the same component — a moderator can log, edit, and delete many harvests against one produce, and the two forms can't drift apart again.

That change also needed an API fix, because the moderator's `PUT` route used to rewrite the newest `harvests` row from the form's harvest-date field. Left as-is, saving the form would have silently undone a pick the moderator had just logged in the panel. The route now only touches harvests when a caller actually sends a harvest date — which only the create flow does, to seed the first harvest — mirroring the farmer's update-listing route, which never touches harvests at all.

**"Some items are missing"** — I checked this field by field against the farmer's produce form and could not find a genuine gap. Every field the farmer saves is on the moderator form: name, variety, method, category, unit, stock, brix, shelf life, the three price tiers, delivery mode with charge and radius, soil organic carbon, soil pH, pesticide result, description, cover photo, and the extra-photo gallery. The one field that looked missing at first, `how_we_grow`, turned out to be a red herring: on the produce form it has no input on *either* side (it's carried through on save so it isn't wiped), and where it *is* editable — the farmer profile — the moderator already has it in `ModeratorFarmerForm`. So the missing item the client saw was the harvest logger itself.

`npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and `npm run build` succeeds.

## What I'd suggest next

The code is done but unverified against a real moderator session, and it's still uncommitted. Yes — this one is fixed too, in the same uncommitted batch. That's the important caveat: the client is hitting this on `gogrameen.in`, and production deploys from `main`, so **the fix is written but not yet shipped**. Nothing you've built for either card is live.

## What was actually wrong

The farmer dashboard had two different ideas of "am I logged in." Page rendering trusted `localStorage` (the farmer's id, cached so pages can query Supabase without a round-trip), but every write endpoint — `ship`, `confirm-pickup`, `deliver`, `acknowledge`, `decline` — checks the HTTP-only `yff_farmer` cookie. Those drift apart: the cookie hits its 30-day expiry or the browser drops it, while `localStorage` holds the id forever. The farmer then gets a dashboard that looks completely normal, renders their real orders, and answers "Please log in." on every single button — exactly the screenshots on the card, where the alert fires on Mark Shipped and the inline error appears under Confirm.

## How the working tree fixes it

The cookie is now the only authority on session state, and `localStorage` is demoted to a pure cache. A new `src/lib/farmer-auth-client.ts` provides the two entry points that close the drift: `requireFarmerSession()` runs on page load and verifies the cached id against `/api/auth/me`, and `farmerFetch()` wraps every write so a 401 sends the farmer to the login page (with a "your session ended" notice and a `next` param back to where they were) instead of leaving them on a dead screen. All five order actions now call `farmerFetch`, so there is no remaining path that can produce the old behavior.

Two supporting fixes came with it. The session cookie now slides its 30-day window on `/api/auth/me` once a token is a day old, so an active farmer never expires mid-order — that's the root cause, not just the symptom. And there's a new `/api/auth/logout` route, because clearing `localStorage` client-side never dropped the HTTP-only cookie, so "logout" wasn't really logging anyone out.

The order-detail page is read-only (no action buttons), so it only needed the session check, which it has.

## Where that leaves you

Both Trello cards — the moderator harvest sync and this login bug — are complete in the working tree, typecheck clean, and build green. Neither is committed, so neither is on the client's site. The login bug is the more urgent of the two, since it's blocking farmers from fulfilling real orders in production right now.

I'd suggest committing both and deploying. Want me to commit, and do you want the two cards as separate commits or one batch? I'll hold off on pushing until you confirm.

1	// Harvest model helpers — the "Harvested 2 hours ago" clock and freshness math.
2	// A produce_listing is the template; a `harvests` row is one actual pick with a
3	// harvested_at timestamp + shelf_life_days. See scripts/harvests-migration.sql.
4	
5	export type Harvest = {
6	  id: string
7	  produce_listing_id: string
8	  farmer_id?: string | null
9	  harvested_at: string
10	  shelf_life_days?: number | null
11	  approx_quantity?: number | null
12	  unit?: string | null
13	  notes?: string | null
14	}
15	
16	type Tr = (en: string, te: string) => string
17	const en: Tr = (e) => e
18	
19	// Local midnight (start of the calendar day) for a given time, so day-level
20	// differences are counted by the calendar — "yesterday" means the previous
21	// calendar day — not by elapsed 24-hour chunks. Without this, a pick from the
22	// 5th at 4pm viewed on the 7th at 10am (42h) would round to 1 → "yesterday",
23	// when a person reading the dates expects "2 days ago".
24	function startOfLocalDay(ms: number): number {
25	  const d = new Date(ms)
26	  d.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0)
27	  return d.getTime()
28	}
29	
30	// "just now" / "12 min ago" / "2 hours ago" / "yesterday" / "3 days ago".
31	// For a future harvest (farmer logged an upcoming pick) → "in 2 hours" etc.
32	function relTime(iso: string, L: Tr): string {
33	  const then = new Date(iso).getTime()
34	  if (isNaN(then)) return ''
35	  const now = Date.now()
36	  const diffMs = now - then
37	  const future = diffMs < 0
38	  const mins = Math.floor(Math.abs(diffMs) / 60000)
39	
40	  if (mins < 1) return L('just now', 'ఇప్పుడే')
41	  const fmt = (n: number, unitEn: string, unitTe: string) =>
42	    future
43	      ? `${L('in', 'లో')} ${n} ${L(unitEn, unitTe)}`
44	      : `${n} ${L(unitEn, unitTe)} ${L('ago', 'క్రితం')}`
45	
46	  if (mins < 60) return fmt(mins, mins === 1 ? 'min' : 'mins', 'నిమి')
47	
48	  // Day buckets are counted by calendar days, not 24-hour spans. Within the
49	  // same calendar day we still show hours ("5 hours ago"); once the date rolls
50	  // over it's "yesterday", "2 days ago", etc.
51	  const dayDiff = Math.round((startOfLocalDay(now) - startOfLocalDay(then)) / 86_400_000)
52	  if (dayDiff === 0) {
53	    const hrs = Math.floor(mins / 60)
54	    return fmt(hrs, hrs === 1 ? 'hour' : 'hours', 'గం')
55	  }
56	  if (dayDiff === 1) return L('yesterday', 'నిన్న')
57	  if (dayDiff === -1) return L('tomorrow', 'రేపు')
58	  return fmt(Math.abs(dayDiff), 'days', 'రోజులు')
59	}
60	
61	// The headline clock shown on a harvest, e.g. "🌾 Harvested 2 hours ago".
62	export function harvestClock(harvestedAt: string, L: Tr = en): string {
63	  const rel = relTime(harvestedAt, L)
64	  if (!rel) return ''
65	  const future = new Date(harvestedAt).getTime() > Date.now()
66	  return future
67	    ? `${L('Harvest expected', 'కోత అంచనా')} ${rel}`
68	    : `${L('Harvested', 'కోసింది')} ${rel}`
69	}
70	
71	// Calendar days a harvest has been off the plant. Day 0 = picked today, 1 =
72	// yesterday, etc. Counted by calendar date (not elapsed 24-hour chunks) so it
73	// stays consistent with the "Harvested N days ago" clock above.
74	export function harvestAgeDays(harvestedAt: string): number {
75	  const then = new Date(harvestedAt).getTime()
76	  if (isNaN(then) || then > Date.now()) return 0
77	  return Math.max(0, Math.round((startOfLocalDay(Date.now()) - startOfLocalDay(then)) / 86_400_000))
78	}
79	
80	// Freshness from shelf life: days left before it spoils, and whether it's past.
81	// Returns null when no shelf life is set (can't compute).
82	export function freshnessLeftDays(harvestedAt: string, shelfLifeDays?: number | null): number | null {
83	  if (shelfLifeDays == null || shelfLifeDays <= 0) return null
84	  const left = shelfLifeDays - harvestAgeDays(harvestedAt)
85	  return left
86	}
87	
88	// Short freshness label, e.g. "3 days fresh left" / "Use today" / "Past best".
89	export function freshnessLabel(harvestedAt: string, shelfLifeDays?: number | null, L: Tr = en): string | null {

95	  return `${left} ${L('days fresh left', 'రోజులు తాజా')}`

## The sections were there — they just had nothing to show

Both tables *are* mounted on the consumer page and RLS is fine. They're built to render nothing when they match zero harvests, and that's exactly what was happening. The cause was the definition of "fresh": the query hardcoded **picked within the last 2 days**, but every harvest in your production database is older than that. The newest is a Papaya at 4.1 days. So the Fresh table matched zero rows and hid itself, which reads to the client as "the section is missing."

That 2-day rule also contradicted the rest of the app. Your harvests carry a `shelf_life_days` — Papaya keeps 5 days, Turmeric Powder 30 — and the harvest detail page already tells buyers "3 days fresh left" from it. But the home page would hide that same turmeric on day 3 of 30, while the product page called it fresh.

**The fix:** freshness now follows shelf life, using `freshnessLeftDays()` — the same helper behind the "days fresh left" label — so there's one definition of fresh instead of two. Postgres can't compare a row against its own shelf-life column through PostgREST, so the query over-fetches a wide window and filters in the component. I also excluded sold-out harvests, since every row in that table has an add-to-cart button.

Against your real data, **Fresh Harvests now renders with the Papaya** (4.1 days old, 5-day shelf, 16 in stock). The three Bananas and the Turmeric stay hidden — they're genuinely past their shelf life, so that's correct, not a bug. Typecheck is clean.

## One thing I need you to decide

**Upcoming Harvests will still not appear**, and no code change will make it. There are zero future-dated harvests in the database — nobody has logged a pick with a date in the future. The table has nothing to list.

So the section is behaving correctly, but the client will keep reporting it missing until a farmer pre-books a harvest.
